Man Buys New 2026 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 for $236,760, Drives 2,300 Miles, Sells for $262,000
29 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
We're still waiting for used C8 ZR1 prices to fall below MSRP, and while that hasn't happened yet, we're definitely getting closer. We've already seen several examples sell for relatively modest premiums, including a 2027 ZR1 Convertible that fetched just $7,600 over sticker back in September.
In the case of this particular 2026MY ZR1 Convertible, it recently sold for $262,000 at auction, and the original MSRP was $236,760. So roughly $25,000 over sticker, before other expenses. This is still a healthy premium, especially since this car already covered 2,300 miles - good for the seller, it means they drove it instead of just staring at it.
Then again, we are dealing with a fully loaded ZR1 Convertible , finished in Sebring Orange Tintcoat, which might not be my first choice in terms of colorways, but it also wouldn't be my last. The car looks great. Let's put it this way - an outrageous-looking Vette should have a vibrant color.
Other exterior-related highlights include the Carbon Flash dual racing stripes, the carbon fiber high rear wing, front dive planes, hood-mounted Gurney flap, mirror caps, plus the LED headlights, front and rear cameras, and the set of Carbon Flash 20" and 21" forged wheels with Michelin Pilot Sport 4S rubber and carbon ceramic discs with orange-finished calipers. There's also a front-axle lift system, as you'd expect to find on just about any ZR1/ZR1X.
Moving along to the interior, that's where you'll find the Habanero and Jet Black upholstery, carbon fiber trim, heated and ventilated GT2 bucket seats, ZR1 door-sill covers, keyless entry, a performance data and video recorder, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a Bose sound system, head-up display, a carbon fiber-trimmed steering wheel, and a wide range of electronic driver aids such as lane-keep assist, rear cross-traffic alert, side blind-zone alert, and forward collision alert.
Photo: Bring a Trailer As for performance, we're dealing with a mid-mounted twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter LT7 V8 , pushing 1,064 horsepower and 828 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic. According to GM, you can hit 60 mph (97 kph) in just 2.3 seconds behind the wheel of the new ZR1, but that's with a one-foot rollout.
The top speed is even more impressive at 233 mph (375 kph). That's hypercar territory for way less than what you'd pay for something with a more exotic badge. At this point, the only reason why you'd pay for a McLaren or Ferrari is exclusively because of the badge.
Look, value-wise, the ZR1 is a fascinating proposition. But I think I'd rather wait another year or so and see where prices settle. We're already seeing relatively small premiums, so it goes without saying that used models will eventually trade below MSRP. Can you imagine? A 1,064 horsepower Corvette for around $200,000? Delicious.
